name: Coast Guard white with the racing stripe
description: Overall white with a black radome. The racing stripe across the forward fuselage behind the flight deck, leaning forward: a broad orange band, a narrow white gap and a thin blue stripe aft of it, from the crown down to the belly, the Coast Guard's emblem on the orange. The aircraft's number in black capitals below the cockpit windows, 'U.S. COAST GUARD' in black block capitals along the aft fuselage behind the wing. On the fin, under a white tip, an orange panel from near the leading edge back to the rudder, a white band with the national insignia in full color, and an orange band at the root; the rudder white, a black panel at the root of the leading edge. Measured on the HC-130J; the HC-144 and HC-27J wear the same scheme.

logos.description: The Coast Guard's emblem on the orange band: crossed anchors behind a ringed disc, the shield in it (our own simplified mark).
The national insignia in full color on the fin's white band: a white star on a blue disc, white bars with a red stripe, outlined in blue.

titles.style: Black block capitals along the aft fuselage behind the wing, over the main gear's sponson.
The aircraft's own number (2002 in the measuring photo) in black capitals below the cockpit windows, ahead of the stripe; its air station's name in small capitals under it (not drawn).

notes:
Measured off the Juneau photo of 2002 (right side, flipped) fitted to shapes/C30J.json: the orange band's forward edge from x 0.115 at the crown to 0.235 at the belly, its aft edge from 0.211 to 0.325, curving (steeper near the belly); the blue stripe 0.6-0.8% of the length wide, a gap of about the same ahead of it; the emblem centered 7.1 m back at the window line, 0.93 m tall; the number from 3.1 to 4.6 m back, its caps 0.35 m tall; 'U.S. COAST' running forward from 21.95 m back, 0.42 m caps, so the whole title (16 letters and spaces at that pitch) from about 14.6 m: the start under the wing is extrapolated (no photo shows it unhidden by the nacelles). The fin's panels by their heights (the orange panel from 0.375 to 0.94 of the fin's height, the white band from 0.155, the root band below), their aft edge the rudder's hinge as the shape places it (x 0.75), the white leading-edge strip about 0.25 m. The orange is sampled from the photos in shade and sun; the Coast Guard's aircraft stripe is often given as International Orange, not confirmed here. The number is the aircraft's own (`registration`): each airframe letters its own, which an app with the aircraft's registration draws in its place. The Coast Guard's HC-144 (CN-235) and HC-27J (C-27J) wear the same scheme, drawn on their own shapes when measured; its HC-130Hs (retired) and its helicopters are left out. The black radome (2026-11-22) as the photos show it, larger than the drawn C-130A's joint: from the crown at the forehead 1.17 m back, its joint slanting down and back to 1.70 m back just under the middle, then straight down to the belly (Juneau's photo puts it 1.75-1.84 m back, taken a little from ahead; Barbers Point's and Grand Forks' about 0.4 m ahead of the side window): `radome.to` up to the forehead, the rest an area.
The HC-144 (CN-235, types.CN35): The Coast Guard's white scheme on the HC-144 Ocean Sentry (CN-235-300 MP), as on the HC-130J (UCG/standard) with its own placement. Overall white, a small black radome cap. The racing stripe leaning forward across the forward fuselage just behind the flight deck: a broad orange band, a narrow white gap and a thin blue stripe aft of it, from the crown to the belly, the emblem on the orange at the window line. The aircraft's number in black below and behind the cockpit windows, ahead of the stripe (its air station's name in small capitals under it, not drawn); 'U.S. COAST GUARD' in black block capitals high on the aft fuselage, behind the wing and ahead of the fin. On the fin, behind a black leading-edge boot and a white strip: an orange panel from under a white tip down to a white band with the national insignia, and an orange panel below it to the root; the rudder white. Cabin windows not drawn (the HC-144 has two a side, the CN-235's transport row is plugged). Measured off the Opa-locka photo of 2311 (right side, flipped) fitted to shapes/CN35.json. Each of the stripe's four edges was traced at 9-14 heights and fitted as a straight line in side view (within 0.004 of the length), then given one common lean (0.093 of the length from crown to belly, as all four measure within 0.002): the orange band's forward edge from x 0.121 at the crown to 0.214 at the belly, 1.45 m wide; the white gap 0.14 m; the blue stripe 0.22 m. The radar radome under the forward fuselage hides the stripe's lowest part (carried to the belly). The emblem centered 4.34 m back at the window line, 0.62 m tall; the number from 2.17 to 3.05 m back, its caps 0.27 m; 'U.S. COAST GUARD' from 13.1 to 16.5 m back, its caps 0.27 m. On the fin (fin space): the black boot about 0.06 of the chord from 0.35 of the height to the tip, a white strip behind it; the upper orange panel from 0.505 to 0.95 of the height, its aft edge the rudder's hinge (0.60-0.66); the white band 0.35-0.505 with the insignia; the lower orange panel to the root, reaching the leading edge below 0.29; the white tip above 0.95; the rudder white. Against the HC-130J (UCG/standard): the stripe is further forward (just behind the cockpit, 2.6-6.4 m back against the C-130J's 3.8-9.8 m) and leans the same way; the number is ahead of the stripe under the cockpit on both; the title sits high on the aft fuselage ahead of the fin (on the C-130J, lower, over the sponson); the fin has no white rudder band but a white rudder throughout, a black boot the length of the leading edge, and no black root panel. Not drawn: the wings' orange outer panels and gray band on top, 'USCG' and the insignia on the wings (a scheme's wing marks aren't placed on top), the orange panels on the tailplane's outer forward chord (both faces), the red propeller warning line, the forward exit's and paratroop door's orange outlines, the radar radome's and FLIR turret's black, and 'HC-144B' with the number under the tailplane's leading edge. The HC-144A of 2007 had an orange rudder; 2311 (2023) and 2315 (2025) have it white, as drawn.
